influences.name: Neil Young
influences.context: Like Neil Young before him, White deals in aural extremes — both Godzilla-scaled rock songs and tender, innocent balladry.

influences.name: The Cramps
influences.context: featuring a characteristically harebrained solo from a tangle-headed, Cramps-shirted White

influences.name: Roger Daltrey
influences.context: he lets loose a Roger Daltrey-style, full-chested, life-affirming "Yeeeeeeeeeah!!!"

influences.name: Paul McCartney
influences.context: The tender, solitary "You've Got Her in Your Pocket" displays White's mastery of McCartney-style sentimentality.

influences.name: Robert Johnson
influences.context: Therein, originals like "The Big Three Killed My Baby" and "Astro" stand toe-to-toe with the traditional tunes "John the Revelator" (interpolated into "Cannon") and "St. James Infirmary Blues," Robert Johnson's "Stop Breaking Down"

influences.name: Bob Dylan
influences.context: Therein, originals like "The Big Three Killed My Baby" and "Astro" stand toe-to-toe with the traditional tunes "John the Revelator" (interpolated into "Cannon") and "St. James Infirmary Blues," Robert Johnson's "Stop Breaking Down" and Bob Dylan's "One More Cup of Coffee."

influences.name: Ray Davies
influences.context: White indulged his inner Ray Davies in the sunshiney "Apple Blossom"

influences.name: Blind Willie McTell
influences.context: It all ends with "Your Southern Can is Mine," one of many casual, tongue-in-cheek album closers for the Stripes — this one borrowed from White's hero Blind Willie McTell.

influences.name: The Rolling Stones
influences.context: It's no wonder White previously joined the Stones onstage for "Loving Cup."

influences.name: Nicki Minaj
influences.context: inspired by rappers like Nicki Minaj, White made the album in an isolated frenzy

influences.name: Mitch Easter
influences.context: Joshua V Smith discovered Fidelitorium Recordings, owned and run by Mitch Easter, who worked on REM's early albums. Observing and assisting Easter for a number of years awakened a love of analogue gear and working methods in Smith.
